title: add rag ci smokekit and local event-simulator quickstart
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: teams building RAG pipelines need reproducible CI smoke tests and a lightweight local event simulator to validate prompt/tool-calling behavior across model rollouts. This PR introduces a small, self-contained quickstart that wires together: 1) a reproducible CI 'smokekit' with sample prompts, golden outputs and a lightweight harness for token-level assertions; 2) a local event-simulator that can replay user sessions, tool invocations and vector store retrieval traces; 3) docs site updates and a short 'how-to' for integrating the smokekit into CI pipelines (GitHub Actions) and for running the simulator during local dev. What changed: added quickstarts/rag-ci-smokekit/ with harness, sample prompts, golden assertions and a minimal Dockerfile for CI; added quickstarts/rag-local-sim/ which contains an event-simulator written in Node (TS) that can replay JSON session traces and mock tool endpoints; added docs/quickstarts/rag-ci-smokekit.md with usage, CI snippets and troubleshooting; updated README index to include links. Checklist: - [x] smokekit harness and assertions implemented; - [x] local event simulator with mocked tool endpoints; - [x] docs written and linked; - [x] CI workflow example included (.github/workflows/rag-smokekit.yml); - [x] unit tests for simulator core and smoke assertions. Test plan: run `npm ci && npm test` in rag-local-sim and `python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r quickstarts/rag-ci-smokekit/requirements.txt && pytest` for smokekit harness. To run locally: 1) start simulator `yarn start` which exposes a mock tools port and a replay endpoint; 2) run the quickstart runner which points at the mock endpoints and produces token-level diffs; 3) see docs/quickstarts/rag-ci-smokekit.md for example traces and CI snippets. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes; quickstarts and docs only. Related: references ENG-32114 for CI coverage goals. Notes: the smokekit contains a small golden-output set intentionally tolerant to minor logits variation; CI uses a token similarity metric with a threshold to avoid flaky failures. Rollout: this was merged to main after approvals and green CI.
